scope: Independent source review of the prospective implementation auditor; existing smoke evidence inspected, no prospective observations generated or inspected.
checks: Only complete case prefixes at flushed byte boundaries are accepted; every expected method/replicate identity is required exactly once.
All logged RNG blocks, paid actions, safe nuisance predictions, unequal allocation plans, costs and exact scores are reconstructed.
All eligible screens before the recorded stop use the original full certificate to exclude a missed earlier certified stop.

Every terminal decision is certified. Mechanical first/last replicates, errors and abstentions require the original complete interval; remaining lazy proofs use nonnegative expert partial sums with unchanged thresholds.
Lazy proof counters and full interval counters are distinct; overlapping intervals are not described as reproducing the stored tight interval.
Mechanical first/last and error groups also replay the complete original runner and require exact record equality.
Audited prefix hashes are rechecked against the final ledger, and complete summary and analysis cells are reconstructed without excluding errors or caps.
The paired stratified bootstrap is independently recalculated through multiplicity matrices and explicit linear quantiles.
The final revision adds hard-deadline checks before each trajectory group and original-runner replay; the statistical and numerical review remains unchanged.
limits: Normalizers and original planner functions are reused; this is not a separate theoretical proof of those primitives.
The watcher does not resume existing case audit artifacts after process loss.
A single already-started trajectory group may finish after the deadline check; the process owner must manage the hard wall-clock stop.
A passed prospective audit would not by itself establish theorem novelty or full-field SOTA dominance.
